clue.text: Occasionally 13 with 8?

definitions.meaning: from time to time, at intervals
13 is the millennium, current when the puzzle ran, and 8 is the very beginning of time: the present together with the distant past

explanation.surface: A puzzle-solver is told to combine two other entries every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references point at 13-down and 8-down: a millennium being celebrated is the present moment, the year dot is long ago, so together they are the present and the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done at odd intervals happens sometimes, at this moment and at that one.

clue.text: Cheek by jowl?

definitions.meaning: the part of the body right next to the jowl, the lower jaw

explanation.surface: The phrase cheek by jowl, meaning side by side, given a question mark.
explanation.walkthrough: The familiar phrase cheek by jowl is split: 'Cheek' is sauce or nerve, and 'by jowl' is cryptic for the body part found beside the jaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve or effrontery is also called this, as in having the nerve to ask; the throat region sits just below the jowl.

clue.text: Take turns in section of orchestra

definitions.meaning: to coil or twist round, as a road or a clock spring does
the woodwind and brass players, who blow their instruments

explanation.surface: Orchestral players take turns in their section.
explanation.definitionFit: A twisting road snakes about; flutes, oboes and horns form the blown-instrument department of an orchestra.

clue.text: Cursory description of minor poet's work

definitions.meaning: a word that chimes with the word cursory, so describes it as a rhyme
a minor is a child, so this is verse for or by small children

explanation.surface: A dismissive review of a lesser poet's output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minor poet' looks like an unimportant writer, but a minor is a child. 'Cursory description' plays on nursery being a word that rhymes with cursory.
explanation.definitionFit: Short traditional verses such as Humpty Dumpty are recited to infants.

clue.text: Bird about to be seen in far-flung highland area

indicators.note: the bird is wrapped about the other word, which sits inside it

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird is about to be spotted in a remote mountainous region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to be' reads as 'on the point of being', but 'about' is the container signal, with 'to' and 'seen in' as link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The remote Himalayan plateau north of Nepal is a distant, high-altitude region.

clue.text: Shortened run, to prevent showing off, technically?

indicators.note: the word for a run is cut short by losing its final letter

parts.note: in cricket an extra is a run not scored off the bat, such as a bye or wide
to avert something is to prevent it happening

explanation.surface: A cricket shot curtailed to stop someone grandstanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortened' drops the last A of EXTRA, leaving EXTR, to which AVERT is added. The definition has a question mark because the psychologist's term is only loosely 'showing off'.
explanation.definitionFit: In psychology the outgoing, sociable personality type turns outward and seeks attention, a technical cousin of being a show-off.

clue.text: Stop eating sort of convenience food

definitions.meaning: to go without food, as at Lent or Ramadan
burgers and fries sold quickly are this kind of food

explanation.surface: Advice to give up junk meals.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstaining from meals is a religious observance; takeaway burgers are quick-service food.

clue.text: What sister has to look for later

parts.note: to look after someone is to care for them, so after goes with look for
a hospital sister is a senior nurse in charge of wards

explanation.surface: A senior nurse's duty is to look after her hospital wards.
explanation.walkthrough: In British hospitals a sister is a senior nurse who runs a ward; the surface hides the phrase 'look after wards'.
explanation.definitionFit: Subsequently, at a time following some event, means the same as later.

clue.text: Article ready for editing, up to date, one imagines

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: the words are ready to be edited, so their letters are to be reworked

parts.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece prepared for the subeditor and bang up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up to date' reads as current, but 'up' is only a link and 'date, one imagines' is the definition: a jocular imagined date when time began.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a jocular name for an imagined, impossibly ancient date at the very start of history.

clue.text: Give prisoner an excellent reference

parts.note: con is slang for a convict
a tribute is a warm statement of praise

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to provide a convict with a glowing character reference.
explanation.definitionFit: To donate or chip in something to a common cause is to give it.

clue.text: Left out of fashion, in a nasty spot

indicators.note: the letter for left is taken out of the word for fashion

parts.note: style is fashion or vogue

explanation.surface: Someone left unfashionable finds themselves in an awkward situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a nasty spot' looks like a tricky situation, but it is a pimple-like swelling on the eyelid.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflamed swelling on the edge of the eyelid is a painful blemish.

clue.text: People regarded as thick may ring this bell

definitions.text: People regarded as thick may ring this bell

parts.words: People regarded as thick may ring this bell
parts.note: people as thick as thieves are thieves, and a thief breaking in sets off the warning bell on a house

explanation.surface: Stupid people might telephone or recognise this bell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thick' suggests stupid, but recalls 'as thick as thieves'; the intruders are those who set the bell ringing.
explanation.definitionFit: A house siren sounds when an intruder trips it.

clue.text: It was said to explain shortage of clues with greater complexity

definitions.text: It was said to explain shortage

indicators.note: the words are made more complex, their letters tangled into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A setter excuses having few clues by making them harder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with greater complexity' reads as more difficult clues, but CLUES and GREATER are the fodder that 'complexity' rearranges; 'with' links them.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase 'that's war' was a shrug offered in wartime for scarcities and hardships.

clue.text: The end of a grand celebration?

definitions.text: The end of a grand celebration?

parts.words: The end of a grand celebration?
parts.note: a grand is a thousand, so this marks the close of a thousand-year span, celebrated with fireworks

explanation.surface: The finale of a big party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand' looks like 'impressive', but it is slang for a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousand-year period was marked by worldwide festivities when its count turned over in 2000.

clue.text: Barge in flailing baton, ducking missile

indicators.note: the missile ducks down into the anagram, placed inside it
the baton waves wildly about, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder
an arrow is a missile shot from a bow

explanation.surface: Someone barges in waving a baton about and dodging a projectile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barge' looks like a verb but is the noun; 'flailing' signals the anagram and 'ducking' the insertion of the missile.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, slim canal boat is a type of barge.

clue.text: Where customs may search, whatever happens

definitions.meaning: customs officers look inside travellers' suitcases

explanation.surface: Customs officials searching luggage come what may.
explanation.definitionFit: Inside some piece of luggage is where officials look; the phrase also means anyhow.

clue.text: Original stimulation offered for the consumer

definitions.text: Original stimulation offered for the consumer

parts.words: Original stimulation offered for the consumer
parts.note: a diner is offered a small first course to stimulate hunger before the main meal

explanation.surface: A marketing incentive for shoppers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumer' suggests a shopper, but here it is someone consuming food; 'Original' means first.
explanation.definitionFit: A starter served before a meal whets the diner's hunger.

clue.text: Good place to hide, being white

parts.note: a lair is an animal's den or a hideout

explanation.surface: A fine hideout that is white.
explanation.walkthrough: 'white' is the white of an egg, which is what this word names, used as a glaze.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg-white used in bookbinding and baking as a glaze is this.

clue.text: Tree by start of left-hand bend

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: an arch is a curve or bend

explanation.surface: A tree beside where a road turns left.
explanation.definitionFit: A deciduous conifer with needles that fall in winter is a kind of tree.

clue.text: Confirm bill's settled for scotch?

definitions.meaning: to stamp the word on an invoice to show it is settled
to scotch something is to put a stop to it

explanation.surface: Proving the bill was paid for a whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scotch' looks like whisky, but means put an end to.
explanation.definitionFit: Marking an invoice settled is the literal sense; the idiom means to finish something off.

clue.text: Original Dutch community finally settled on York

definitions.text: Original Dutch community finally settled on York

parts.words: Original Dutch community finally settled on York
parts.note: the Dutch colony on Manhattan was renamed after the Duke of York when the English took it, so its name ended up as York with the same prefix

explanation.surface: First Dutch settlers chose York as their home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settled' suggests colonists arriving, but means the name was finally fixed: the colony became New York in 1664.
explanation.definitionFit: The seventeenth-century Dutch colonial town on Manhattan carried a Netherlands capital's name before becoming New York.

clue.text: Root out American involved in corruption

indicators.note: the abbreviation for American is wrapped up inside the word for corruption

parts.note: rot is decay or corruption

explanation.surface: Uncovering an American caught up in graft.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse or drive someone out from hiding is to dig them out.

clue.text: Pay for basic support

definitions.meaning: the base on which a body or column stands

explanation.surface: Paying for fundamental aid.
explanation.definitionFit: Settling the bill means covering the cost; the base of a leg or pillar bears weight.

clue.text: Go down for an audition, in time to be in 'it

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as "Go down for an audition, in time to be in 'it" (OCR): SINK sounds like SYNC, but no definition word fits cleanly and "to be in 'it" looks garbled; no scan to check.
annotationWithheld.clue: Go down for an audition, in time to be in 'it

clue.text: Example of 'symbolism one has to study in Shakespeare

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
con is an old word, used by Shakespeare, meaning to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare student finds an example of symbolism.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious image or emblem stands for something greater, a sample of symbolic representation.

clue.text: Jokingly kissing your colt, as it's frisky

indicators.note: a frisky colt jumps about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A playful kiss for your young horse because it is lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jokingly' marks the word as a humorously learned term rather than everyday English.
explanation.definitionFit: This mock-Latinate adjective relates to the act of pressing lips together in affection.

clue.text: Ditching half my theory a false interpretation?

indicators.note: the phrase loses its second half, so only the first half of its letters remain

parts.note: the letters run on across these two words only because keeping the first half of a phrase always leaves its opening letters: a coincidence of the halving, not a separate hiding

explanation.surface: Dropping half of a pet theory as a misreading.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend or popular fallacy is a widely held but untrue belief.

clue.text: It's one's basic skill that counts

definitions.text: It's one's basic skill that counts

parts.words: It's one's basic skill that counts
parts.note: one of the three Rs taught in primary school is the knack of adding and subtracting

explanation.surface: A proverb that only fundamentals matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counts' reads as 'matters' but means doing sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Elementary sums are a fundamental school skill dealing with numbers.
